extracted.intended_audience: ICLR 2022 reviewers (conference peer reviewers, machine learning community)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and procedural rules for serving as a reviewer for ICLR 2022, including how to read, evaluate, write, discuss, and finalize reviews and how to handle ethics, conflicts, and requests for experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely and substantive reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Your reviews are timely and substantive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a constructive, thorough and timely review (dates provided: review and discussion windows). Reviewers will be acknowledged; top reviewers receive special acknowledgement and free registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to Code of Ethics and Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: You must adhere to our Code of Ethics in your role as a reviewer. You must also adhere to our Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the CoE report: check assigned papers for conflicts with the code of ethics and mark them in your review form. If uncertain, reach out to your area chair. Flag CoE violations throughout review and discussion phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the paper thoroughly and check related work
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the paper: It’s important to carefully read through the entire paper, and to look up any related work and citations that will help you comprehensively evaluate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give yourself sufficient time for this step. Consider looking at supplementary material if it answers questions that arise while reading the main paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider the objective of the work
rubrics_metrics.description: While reading, consider the objective of the work: What is the goal of the paper? Is it to better address a known application or problem, draw attention to a new application or problem, or to introduce and/or explain a new theoretical finding? A combination of these?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different objectives require different considerations as to potential value and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify strong points (quality dimensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong points: is the submission clear, technically correct, experimentally rigorous, reproducible, does it present novel findings (e.g. theoretically, algorithmically, etc.)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List and be explicit about specific strengths (e.g., novelty, experimental completeness, dataset contributions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify weak points (quality deficits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Weak points: is it weak in any of the aspects listed in strong points (clarity, correctness, rigor, reproducibility, novelty)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be as comprehensive as possible when listing weaknesses and explain their importance for acceptance decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be mindful of biases and open-minded
rubrics_metrics.description: Be mindful of potential biases and try to be open-minded about the value and interest a paper can hold for the entire ICLR community, even if it may not be very interesting for you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid letting a personal lack of interest be the sole reason for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific question/problem clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the specific question and/or problem tackled by the paper?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as part of deciding whether to recommend accept or reject; ensure the paper clearly states its problem and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach motivation and literature placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the approach well motivated, including being well-placed in the literature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether prior work is cited appropriately and whether the authors justify why their approach is needed compared to existing methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for claims: correctness and rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper support the claims? This includes determining if results, whether theoretical or empirical, are correct and if they are scientifically rigorous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify theoretical arguments, experiments, analyses, reproducibility signals, and whether conclusions follow from results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured review: summarize contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize what the paper claims to contribute. Be positive and generous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear, concise summary helps authors and area chairs quickly understand your interpretation of the paper's claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured review: list strong and weak points
rubrics_metrics.description: List strong and weak points of the paper. Be as comprehensive as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize pros/cons clearly so authors and ACs can see the basis for your recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: State clear recommendation with reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly state your recommendation (accept or reject) with one or two key reasons for this choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the recommendation explicit and tie it directly to the most important evidence or concerns from your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide supporting arguments for recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide supporting arguments for your recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give evidence, point to specific experiments, theoretical results, or missing analyses that justify your decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask clarifying questions for authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask questions you would like answered by the authors to help you clarify your understanding of the paper and provide the additional evidence you need to be confident in your assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the rebuttal period to request targeted clarifications; questions should focus on resolving uncertainties relevant to acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide additional feedback to improve the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide additional feedback with the aim to improve the paper. Make it clear that these points are here to help, and not necessarily part of your decision assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate improvement suggestions from major concerns affecting the accept/reject decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Politeness, precision, and concreteness
rubrics_metrics.description: Be polite in your review. Ask yourself whether you’d be happy to receive a review like the one you wrote. Be precise and concrete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include references to back up any claims, especially claims about novelty and prior work. Constructive tone improves usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: State uncertainties explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: It’s also fine to explicitly state where you are uncertain and what you don’t quite understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifying uncertainties helps authors focus rebuttal and clarifications; may change your recommendation after response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not reject solely for lack of state-of-the-art results or interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t reject a paper just because you don’t find it 'interesting'. This should not be a criterion at all for accepting/rejecting a paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions bring value when they convincingly demonstrate new, relevant, impactful, or insightful knowledge even without SOTA numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage actively in discussion and be responsive
rubrics_metrics.description: During the discussion phase, reviewers, authors and area chairs engage in asynchronous discussion, and authors are allowed to revise their submissions to address concerns that arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is crucial that you are actively engaged and responsive during this phase; you should be able to respond to comments/requests within 3 business days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide final recommendation after discussion and revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide final recommendation: Update your review, taking into account the new information collected during the discussion phase, and any revisions to the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a spirit of openness to changing your initial recommendation (either to a more positive or more negative) rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material policy
rubrics_metrics.description: How should I use supplementary material? It is not necessary to read supplementary material but such material can often answer questions that arise while reading the main paper, so consider looking there before asking authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use judgment on whether supplementary experiments/appendices are necessary for your evaluation; check them when they likely resolve substantive concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling policy violations and ethics concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: How should I handle a policy violation? To flag a CoE violation related to a submission, please indicate it when submitting the CoE report for that paper. The AC will work with the PC and the ethics board to resolve the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To discuss other violations (e.g. plagiarism, double submission, paper length, formatting, etc.), contact either the AC or the PC as appropriate by sending an official comment with the appropriate readership restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting additional experiments: justification and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: You can ask for additional experiments, but make sure you justify why they’re necessary to push the paper over the acceptance threshold. New experiments should not significantly change the content of the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requested experiments should be limited in scope and serve to more thoroughly validate existing results from the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contemporaneous citation guidance (recent work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are authors expected to cite and compare with very recent work? We consider papers contemporaneous if they are published (available in online proceedings) within the last four months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to cite and discuss all relevant papers, but may be excused for not knowing about papers not published in peer-reviewed conference proceedings or journals (including arXiv-only). Reviewers should use good judgement and consult the area chair if in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict-of-interest avoidance and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: How can I avoid being assigned papers that present a conflict of interest? Conflicts are detected using your OpenReview profile information (co-authors, past and current institutions, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update your OpenReview profile. If you find a conflicted paper while bidding, bid 'Very Low'. If assigned a conflicted paper, contact the program chairs immediately to have it re-assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative reviewer tasks and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Main reviewer tasks and dates: create your OpenReview profile and link your DBLP profile (by September 15th 2021); bid on papers (7 Oct - 12 Oct 2021); write review (14 Oct - 1 Nov 2021); discuss with authors/other reviewers/ACs (9 Nov - 29 Nov 2021); provide final recommendation to area chair (by 29 Nov 2021); flag CoE violations throughout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the listed timeline and submit required forms (CoE report) and recommendations by the stated deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to contact the Area Chair
rubrics_metrics.description: To contact the AC for a paper: (i) go to the OpenReview page for that paper (while being logged into OpenReview); (ii) click the button to add an official comment and fill out the comment form; (iii) add the ACs to the list of 'Readers'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the official OpenReview comment mechanism and readership settings to reach ACs appropriately.
